entries.title: Washington's Bitter, Partisan Restaurant Divide — With Data
entries.summary: Federal election filings show Republicans and Democrats eating true to form: Steak for the GOP, while Dems favor the multicultural.
entries.content:
Republicans and Democrats are divided over almost everything in Washington. That includes where to eat.

The Washington Sun analyzed more than 1.6 million Federal Election Commission operating-expenditure records and identified 829 restaurants in the D.C. area where campaigns plunked down over $9 million during the 2026 election cycle from Jan. 1, 2025, through Aug. 11, 2026.

Not only does the culinary campaign survey confirm the hyper-partisan vibe around the capital these days, it also finds the parties noshing true to their stereotypes: red meat for Republicans while Democrats’ choices for blue plate specials have a multicultural flavor.

Republican campaigns reported spending over half a million dollars at The Capital Grille in the Washington area this cycle, making the steakhouse their prime choice by a wide margin. Other GOP favorites include Joe’s Seafood, Ocean Prime, Trattoria Alberto and Bobby Van’s restaurants.

Democrats reported spending the most at Paraiso, a Mexican restaurant and mezcaleria on Capitol Hill, and also delivering hearty portions of cash to Osteria Morini, Ama, L’Ardente and Bistro Cacao.

Tom Sietsema, The Sun’s legendary food critic, took a look at the data and divined that the parties’ hotspots can be explained by two things: “convenience and proximity to power.”

“It doesn’t hurt that Cap Grille, Joe’s and Bobby Van’s are close to the halls of power (either the Hill or the White House),” he said. But as a diner, Sietsema said he’d prefer the Democrats’ usual haunts over “the less imaginative GOP restaurants.”
https://datawrapper.dwcdn.net/maL6u/1/“The best places, food-wise, are Osteria Morini, L’Ardente and Del Mar on the Wharf,” Sietsema wrote. “There’s an Italian/Mediterranean affection going on with the Dems’ list. Carmine’s is BIG, a plus for large groups.”

Democrats spent over $62,000 at Del Mar, a Spanish seafood restaurant. The two parties split around $150,000 roughly right down the middle at Carmine’s, an Italian restaurant in Penn Quarter.

One current senior GOP aide agreed with Sietsema that proximity (with a private event space) is an essential component for campaigns and lawmakers, but added: “I just think Republicans like steak.”

The places where the partisans dine don’t just reveal cultural affinities. They also reflect who has the money and the power.
https://datawrapper.dwcdn.net/TQt2v/1/Republicans, who control Congress and whose party committees have been hauling in more campaign cash than Democrats this cycle, reported dropping substantially more operating expenditures at restaurants in the Washington area, roughly $5 million compared with around $3.9 million for Democrats.

The gap can’t be explained by there being more GOP campaign committees in the analysis: 330 Republican campaigns reported qualifying restaurant spending, compared with 329 on the Democratic side.

The numbers pencil out to roughly $15,300 per Republican group and about $11,900 per Democratic committee. Republican campaigns were also more concentrated in their favorite restaurants: The 10 spots where they reported the most money accounted for nearly 41% of all GOP spending captured by the analysis. In food, as in 2026 politics, Democrats had a bigger tent, with their top 10 locations accounting for just 29% of their expenditures.
https://datawrapper.dwcdn.net/pXlyb/1/The biggest spenders at restaurants are some of the most powerful and ambitious people in Washington. The campaign of House Majority Leader Steve Scalise, who has been aggressively stumping for other Republicans and hopes to keep his leadership post, leads the pack, spending nearly $517,000 at 79 identifiable establishments around D.C. His favorite was Ocean Prime, where the Louisiana Republican spent nearly $117,000 — more than some campaigns spent at all restaurants combined.

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries is the big spender on the Democratic side, with his campaign doling out more than $160,000 across 31 restaurants. The New Yorker spent nearly $45,000 at Osteria Morini, an Italian spot in Navy Yard. Sen. Mark Warner (D-Virginia) was close behind the minority leader at about $149,000, including nearly $25,000 at L’Ardente.

Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer’s campaign spent nearly $100,000 — more than $86,000 of it at Franklin Hall, largely on reception, catering and facility costs.

Osteria Morini, Jeffries’ favorite spot, has a history with Democratic leadership, serving as a longtime destination for former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi’s political and fundraising operations. Pelosi hosted House Democrats there in 2018 when she was campaigning to become speaker again, and a Washingtonian analysis found her campaign spent $26,800 at the Navy Yard eatery during the 2022 cycle.

Democrats are watching to see how Jeffries uses the restaurant circuit if he becomes speaker next year.

“I’m interested to see what [Jeffries’] strategies are when it comes to these kinds of things,” David Thomas, a top Democratic strategist who is a partner at Mehlman Consulting, told The Sun. “When Pelosi was doing it, she obviously would host events, but she also spent a lot of time visiting other members’ events and helping her caucus. She was a great draw for any event. I suspect he will do something similar.”

Thomas, however, admitted he frequently finds himself behind enemy lines. Ocean Prime, where Republicans spent about $210,000, is under his office. He calls it his "satellite office.”

“We’re pretty lucky in D.C. to have an amazing restaurant scene where you’ve got so many different options of places that aren’t just good restaurants, but are able to host events,” Thomas said.

Sean Kennedy, the National Restaurant Association’s chief advocate officer, said large “heavy hitter” restaurants in Washington are experts at meeting the strict schedule demands of members of Congress, but that “there are lobbyists who do get tired of eating at the same restaurant five nights a week.” Kennedy argued fundraising in new locations can be a hook to draw guests.

“There are members of Congress that do smaller events with a smaller number of people, and they move into smaller restaurants,” Kennedy said. “There are an awful lot of smaller folks that are consistently getting tables for six, eight and 10 that exemplify the diversity of the cuisine coming to D.C.”

The spending does not necessarily mean that campaigns were sitting down for dinner every time they booked a restaurant. Often it is for fundraising and catered events.
https://datawrapper.dwcdn.net/QSIOC/1/The Sun carried out its analysis using payments reported to the FEC as operating expenditures, the standard category reported for ordinary campaign expenses, and counted spending when the recipient could be identified as a specific restaurant or other establishment with prepared-food service. The analysis excluded caterers, delivery-only businesses, event venues, retailers and other vendors that could not be tied to a qualifying restaurant. Campaign committees sometimes report restaurant, meal or catering payments under other FEC disbursement categories; those payments are not included in the analysis.

entries.title: How Payment Will Work on the Upcoming Purple Line
entries.summary: The mostly aboveground train system will stretch 16 miles east to west with 21 stations along the way.
entries.content:
There are still many unknowns about the Purple Line, the light-rail train that will connect Bethesda to New Carrollton. The opening date is up in the air. The construction hasn’t finished. The cost for riders has yet to be finalized.

But one thing is for sure: It won’t be free. Some future riders have wondered what payment will look like.

When it comes time to pay, riders will be able to use Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority SmartTrip cards or the Maryland Transit Administration’s CharmPass mobile app, the Maryland Transit Administration told The Washington Sun. Riders can also use cash or a credit card to purchase tickets at vending machines located at each of the line's 21 stops.

Trains won’t have entry or exit faregates, and tickets will be a flat rate, not charged based on distance like Metro rail travel. The actual cost per ride has yet to be decided, according to MTA.

The mostly aboveground train system will stretch 16 miles east to west with 21 stations along the way. The final piece of track was laid in the spring, and construction was 92% complete as of Wednesday.

While the contractual opening date is slated for Dec. 30, 2027, there’s a chance the line doesn't open until 2028. Ray Biggs, senior project director at the Maryland Transit Administration, which will run the Purple Line, told the Montgomery County Council’s Transportation and Environment Committee on Monday that the opening date remains “dynamic.”

entries.title: FDA Says Its Safety Review of Abortion Pill Will Continue Into Next Year
entries.summary: In addition to the safety study, the agency said it is considering a number of petitions proposing changes to how mifepristone is prescribed and distributed.
entries.content:
By Matthew Perrone

WASHINGTON (AP) — The Food and Drug Administration says its ongoing safety review of the nation's main abortion pill will continue into next year, a timeline that was quickly condemned by abortion opponents hoping to see the drug's use curtailed.

The FDA gave a court-ordered update on its progress in a legal filing late Wednesday, providing the first substantive information about the controversial reevaluation ordered by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.

Mifepristone was first approved by the FDA in 2000. The agency has repeatedly reaffirmed the pill’s safety and effectiveness over the years, in addition to easing a number of restrictions on the drug, including dropping a requirement that it be dispensed in person.

But since President Donald Trump returned to the White House, anti-abortion groups and their allies in Congress have pushed the administration to revisit the pill, in the hopes of restricting its use.

The FDA said in its filing that it expects to complete a safety study of the pill by mid-December this year. A report on the findings is expected “no later than March 2027,” after which the agency will decide whether to impose new restrictions or other changes on the drug's use.

Gavin Oxley of Americans United for Life, an anti-abortion group, criticized the move as a lack of “true leadership” by Trump administration officials.

“The administration continues to find itself on the wrong side of women's health, clearly uninterested in mitigating the ongoing harms caused by the abortion pill,” Oxley said.

The two-drug regimen of mifepristone, combined with a second drug misoprostol, is the most common form of abortion in the U.S.

The FDA was directed to provide the latest update by a federal judge in a case brought by the state of Louisiana alleging that mail-delivery of mifepristone undermines the state’s abortion ban. It’s one of several state lawsuits related to mifepristone winding their way through the courts.

Last month a three-judge panel for the 5th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals questioned the merits of Louisiana’s case, including whether the state had the legal standing to challenge FDA’s oversight of mifepristone.

Any ruling from the 5th Circuit on the Louisiana case would not immediately change the landscape because the Supreme Court has blocked changes to the drug until it sees the case again.

The FDA said Wednesday it is using a “statistical data mining method” to discover “unknown safety concerns,” that may exist with the drug. The data comes from an electronic database that collects reports of medical injuries and drug side effects from major health networks and insurers.

In addition to the safety study, the agency said it is considering a number of petitions proposing changes to how mifepristone is prescribed and distributed.

Abortion opponents have focused most of their efforts on a 2021 decision allowing doctors to prescribe the drug online and send it through the mail during COVID-19. That decision, made permanent under President Joe Biden in 2023, had the effect of undermining a number of state abortion bans, since women can receive the drug through the mail.

entries.title: The Capitals Flexed Their Depth in Alex Ovechkin’s Final Home Opener
entries.summary: In his 101st meeting with Sidney Crosby, Ovechkin didn’t need to do much in a 5-3 win over Pittsburgh.
entries.content:
The NHL schedule was made with a sense of ceremony — or at least a sense of potential television ratings. So just as the Capitals played their final home game last season against the Penguins, and just as the Capitals will play their final home game this season against the Penguins, the Capitals played their first home game of 2026-27 against the Penguins on Wednesday night.

Alex Ovechkin and Sidney Crosby have been inextricably linked for the past 21 seasons and remain so for season 22. It’s been a long time — long enough to cover more than half their lives, long enough to encompass the entire physical existence of a few teammates, long enough to soften a fierce rivalry into a mutual respect. The cumulative weight of those years was hard to ignore on Wednesday.

It was the 101st meeting between Ovechkin and Crosby, but it was not one in which either star did much to control the action. The Capitals won, 5-3, in a game that showcased their depth.

“You get off the ice, and there’s a lot of talent coming on after you,” said Capitals forward Tom Wilson. “It’s a good feeling.”

Eight different Capitals recorded a point on Wednesday, including big summer acquisitions Alex Tuch and Jordan Kyrou.

That group did not include Ovechkin, but his presence shaped much of the night anyway. (That impact included a smattering of protesters outside Capital One Arena voicing their frustration with Ovechkin’s recent appearance in a political ad supporting the party of Russian President Vladimir Putin.) It was the first game since 41-year-old Ovechkin announced that he would retire at the end of the season. He spent last year as the subject of permanent speculation. There will be none of that for 2026-27: He knows this is goodbye, and his teammates and fans know it, too. That was impossible to escape in his final home opener.

Fans chanted for Ovechkin before the pregame introductions. His young sons, Sergei and Ilya, were given the job of reading off his name and jersey number. (Ovechkin, rarely one for sentimentality, yielded a little bit here: “It was a pretty cool moment,” he said. Wilson, his most established teammate, was more effusive: “You got chills watching him come out. You've just got to try and soak it all in.") The crowd thrummed with anticipation every time he got the puck in the left circle, waiting for the captain to go to work in his office and give them a reason to explode.

Ovechkin shot twice but did not score. His role has shifted in the twilight of his career: Ovechkin averaged just 17 minutes, 27 seconds of ice time last year, the lowest he’d ever recorded with the Capitals, and that number has been lower this year. Ovechkin played 14 minutes, 5 seconds on Wednesday after logging even fewer minutes in each of the first two games of the season. It’s early in the year, of course, and Ovechkin did not play in the preseason while managing some mild injuries. But his job is clearly different than what it used to be. Most notably on Wednesday, when a 5-on-4 became a 5-on-3, Ovechkin came off the ice.

“I’m not going to say that he doesn’t want to be out there, and he’s like, ‘Yay. Thanks, Carbs, for calling me off,’” Capitals coach Spencer Carbery said. “Like, that’s not how it is. But he also is understanding of what we’re trying to accomplish as a team and the great players that he has around him.”

Ovechkin demurred when questioned about his approach.

“For me personally, I just take it game by game,” he said.

Which, incidentally, will include three more games against Crosby and the Penguins.

Some more notes from the win:

  • The Tuch–Pierre-Luc Dubois–Wilson line continues to shine. All three members scored on Wednesday, and Dubois added one assist while Wilson added two. “They were outstanding tonight, right from their first shift,” Carbery said. He was keen on matching them up against Pittsburgh’s top line as much as possible to maximize the clash of Dubois on Crosby: “I really wanted [Dubois] to play against [Crosby] as much as I could.” Crosby finished as a -4 for the first time in four years.  
  • Washington was 1-for-6 on the power play on Wednesday. (They are now 2-for-10 on the man advantage for the season.) But there have been real signs of improvement here — especially on the second unit, which produced that goal on Wednesday, with Ryan Leonard assisted by Jordan Kyrou and Cole Hutson. “Everyone’s moving really well,” Leonard said. “I think we’re doing a really good job reading off each other.” Their puck movement has been notably better from last year. 
  • Wednesday kicked off a stretch of eight home games in three weeks for the Caps. They will go on the road for one game in Raleigh next week against the Hurricanes but will otherwise be entirely at home until the end of October.

entries.title: Bust of Robert F. Kennedy Is Missing From Namesake Stadium
entries.summary: The statue “was removed by an unknown manner” and there is no known suspect.
entries.content:
A bronze bust of Robert F. Kennedy has sat on the lawn outside of the D.C. stadium named for him for decades, even after the venue was decommissioned. Now, it’s gone missing.

The sculpture was last seen in mid-September, according to a police report obtained by The Washington Sun. An employee of Events D.C., the entertainment authority that manages the RFK Stadium campus, reported the bust as stolen on Oct. 1. The disappearance was first reported by The Washington Post.

The statue “was removed by an unknown manner” and there is no known suspect, according to the police report.

The pedestal holding the statue was not taken and has been moved into storage, a spokesperson for Events D.C. told The Sun.

The bust was installed in 1969, around the time the stadium was renamed to honor Kennedy, who was assassinated on the presidential campaign trail in 1968. Artist Robert Berks, known for sculpting a larger 3,000-pound bust of John F. Kennedy on display at the Kennedy Center, created the piece.

Though RFK Stadium hasn't been operational since 2019, the land holds the promise of new beginnings. A new stadium proposed for the same site is expected to open in 2030 as part of a $3.8 billion development plan that will bring the Washington Commanders back to D.C.

entries.title: Trump Commits to a Pause on Iran Attacks Ahead of the Midterms
entries.summary: The president announced on Truth Social that the U.S. is having “productive discussions” with representatives for the country.
entries.content:
President Donald Trump announced Thursday that the U.S. will not attack Iran in the lead up to the midterm elections on Nov. 3, as Republicans struggle to message on high gas prices and rising costs linked to the monthslong conflict.

“We are having productive discussions with the Islamic Republic of Iran,” Trump wrote Thursday on Truth Social.

The president asserted that “Iran is in very bad condition, both Economically and Militarily,” and added that the naval “Blockade will remain in full force and effect, with Oil flowing in Record Numbers of Barrels through the Hormuz Strait.”

The White House asked the Pentagon to develop a list of Iranian targets to strike ahead of the midterms, The Atlantic reported earlier this week — though Trump’s announcement appears to indicate that he does not plan to act on the plans.

The U.S. has not struck Iran in recent weeks, after July brought back two weeks of intense strikes following a relatively unstable ceasefire earlier in the summer.

Republicans are heading into the midterms with the economy as a top-of-mind issue for voters. The price of diesel reached record highs in the end of September, which prompted several Republicans to call for an end to the war.

Trump touted the movement of oil through the Strait of Hormuz, which serves as a key waterway for the global oil supply, in his post announcing the latest pause in attacks. The president said “22 Million Barrels” moved through the strait “last night alone, with not one barrel coming from, or going to, Iran!”

entries.title: Trump Wore a Cheap Suit. His Former Tailor Is Ready to Weigh In.
entries.summary: Joseph Genuardi compared the online frenzy to the hoopla surrounding Barack Obama’s tan suit — an outfit he was also partially responsible for.
entries.content:
Cut him some slacks.

Donald Trump usually speaks off the cuff — but this week, it was hard to ignore his new material.

The president’s reputation for dressing in high-end menswear precedes him — which is why a photo of Trump opening his suit jacket at a rally in Nebraska to reveal the label of low-budget brand Jos. A. Bank stirred up an online frenzy.

Trump has historically been associated with premium suit brands, particularly Brioni, an Italian luxury suitmaker. He wrote in his 2004 book “Trump: How to Get Rich” that he had “tremendous loyalty” to the brand because it supplied the wardrobe for “The Apprentice.” In September 2016, Hope Hicks, Trump’s campaign spokesperson, told The New York Times that he had been wearing Brioni suits in the lead-up to the election and also favored menswear from Brooklyn-based Martin Greenfield Clothiers.

So, naturally, seeing him in what appeared to be an off-the-rack fit inspired a healthy dose of mockery and plenty of memes.

“Jos. A Bank on the President is the biggest recession indicator of all time,” one user wrote Tuesday on X.
https://x.com/atrupar/status/2107444291107000604?s=20The company has long been synonymous with low-cost materials and overseas manufacturing. A 2014 Saturday Night Live commercial parody poked fun at the brand’s image by having the comedians use its suits to wipe up spills, replace diapers and even help start a fire.

Given this background, Joseph Genuardi, a former head tailor at Martin Greenfield who said he previously worked with Trump, was surprised to hear that the president had eschewed his usual luxury tailoring for a more budget-friendly option — a decision that he thought might indicate a last-minute wardrobe emergency.

“My first instinct is that maybe there was a problem with the original suit that he was going to wear,” Genuardi told The Washington Sun. “Like maybe it got damaged, or this was kind of a last-minute adjustment to his wardrobe.”

The White House and Tailored Brands, the parent company of Jos. A. Bank, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Given Joseph A. Bank’s close to 200 stores across the country, “It’s a suit that's much easier to get than, let's say, a luxury Italian-made or custom-made suit if you need it in a pinch,” Genuardi said.

The master tailor worked with Trump before he won the 2016 election and has also fitted other high-profile clients like former President Barack Obama and former New York City Mayor Michael Bloomberg. He left Martin Greenfield in 2016 and started his own business called Genuardi Master Tailor.
White House Departure Trump AP - 26279675897370 (8640x5760, AR: 1.50)While at Martin Greenfield, Genuardi said he dressed Obama during his second term, and he even helped fit the former president for the infamous tan suit that spurred a conservative uproar when Obama sported the beige ensemble during a White House press conference in 2014.

He compared Trump’s Jos. A Bank news cycle to the backlash surrounding that infamous outfit.

“There’s always people who have angles and reasons why they make a big deal about things, that’s probably also the case with President Trump this time around,” Genuardi said. “I try to stay out of that, but I just thought it was funny because [Obama] looked really fantastic in the tan suit.”

As for whether Trump’s turn to cheaper suits is likely a lasting change to his wardrobe, Genuardi is unconvinced.

“President Trump is a man of means, so he’s been around high-quality clothing for many, many years,” Genuardi told The Sun.

“He was particular about getting something that was very, very well made and showed itself as high quality,” he said, adding that Jos. A. Bank suits aren’t “bad for what they are,” but they often do not have the “high-quality ingredients” Trump might be used to.

Luxury menswear from Brioni and Martin Greenfield can cost orders of magnitude more than Jos. A. Bank’s ready-to-wear tailoring. Brioni lists several suits on its site for more than $8,000, while a Martin Greenfield ensemble costs about $1,500. Jos. A. Bank’s catalog, however, includes many options for under $300.
Barack Obama tan suit (5000x3155, AR: 1.58)In Genuardi’s experience dressing several public figures and other high-powered clients, he said they often want to wear luxury items that don’t “stand out too much.”

“Particularly for a president, in my experience, there's always a balance of demonstrating power with your dress, but at the same time also having relatability,” Genuardi said.

Jos. A Bank isn’t the only budget brand that Trump has taken a shine to during his second term. The president has been known to wear and even give those in his inner circle a $145 pair of leather Oxford shoes from Florsheim, a mid-market label that outsources much of its production overseas.

It remains unclear if Trump was trying to send any message with his fashion decision earlier this week. The economy is top of mind for Americans heading into the midterm elections, though the president has repeatedly derided the concept and said Democrats came up with the idea of “affordability” to hurt Republicans.

Some have also pointed out that Trump donning Jos. A. Bank appears to stand in stark contrast to his push to bolster American production — often through sweeping tariffs on goods from other countries. The label on Trump’s suit, captured by photographers at the rally, appears to show that the suit is from the brand’s lower-end line, and not the company’s American-made imprint.

“Jos. A. Bank suits are all made overseas, typically in countries like China and Bangladesh. They carry an associate label called Joseph Abboud, which is made in the United States,” Derek Guy, a men's fashion industry writer and commentator, wrote Tuesday on X. “I wonder why Trump choose the cheap import over the US-made suit.”
trump suit AP - 26167540996363 (3775x2517, AR: 1.50)Tailored Brands reported in a July 2026 registration statement filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission that Vietnam, Indonesia, Bangladesh and China accounted for approximately 60% of its direct product sourcing spend during the 2025 fiscal year.

“We source a significant portion of our products from manufacturers located outside the U.S. and geopolitical tensions, growing uncertainty or changes to trade policies, tariffs, sanctions and import and export regulations may adversely affect our ability to source goods or cause our cost of goods to increase further, which could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations,” the company wrote in the “risk factors” section of the corporate filing.

Jos. A. Bank’s website also includes a section touting its “American bespoke” pieces, with a large banner on the page reading “Made in USA.”

Historically, men searching for a high-end suit would have to look to Europe, according to Genuardi. There aren’t many American tailors or businesses offering the “world-class” tailoring that Genuardi offers in his shop — but he said that the industry is beginning to change.

“I think that typically an American politician would want to, if at all possible, support American makers, but I think that now there's becoming better options here for high-quality menswear, whereas in the recent past there hasn’t always been,” Genuardi told the Sun.

entries.title: Trump Bars Microsoft From Getting Permanent Residency for Foreign Workers
entries.summary: Vice President JD Vance accused the technology giant of abusing a federal program that gives foreign workers access to green cards.
entries.content:
The Trump administration is blocking Microsoft and Adobe from giving foreign workers temporarily living and working in the United States a pathway to permanent residency, accusing the companies of fraud.

The two tech giants are the biggest names among a slate of others in the industry the Trump administration is cutting off from a program that allows companies to apply for green cards for foreign workers on H-1B visas, Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling announced Thursday.

“We are cutting off the head of the snake,” Sonderling said alongside Vice President JD Vance. Vance and other Trump officials have alleged that the companies are using the government’s permanent labor certification program, known as PERM, as a way to hire cheaper labor at the expense of Americans.

Suspending Microsoft’s and Adobe’s access to PERM is an escalation of the Trump administration’s push to not only target illegal immigration but also significantly reduce pathways for legal immigration.

“There has been no company in the United States, unfortunately, that has abused the system more than Microsoft,” Vance said.

The suspended companies will now no longer be able to receive permanent labor certifications.

The majority, 80%, of Microsoft’s H-1B visa applications the past fiscal year were to extend or change the status of current employees, a spokesperson for the company said in a statement.

“Microsoft only files H-1B petitions for those who meet the rigorous standards of this visa category,” the spokesperson said. “We pay our employees some of the highest compensation in the tech sector, and our wages are among the highest of all H-1B filings. We pay our H-1B employees the same as any other employees doing comparable work.”

The Trump administration has repeatedly targeted the H-1B visa program by trying to make employers pay $100,000 fees, which federal judges have struck down.

So far this fiscal year, the Labor Department has issued 104,028 certifications for permanent workers, according to data from the department. The administration issued 138,093 the last fiscal year.

entries.title: Judge Temporarily Extends White House Access for Publications Targeted by Trump
entries.summary: Judge Timothy Kelly issued the extension after both sides argued over whether the outlets violated journalistic standards and infringed on national security.
entries.content:
A U.S. district judge temporarily extended White House access to CNN, MS NOW and Politico following a hearing Thursday on President Donald Trump’s media ban.

Judge Timothy Kelly issued the extension after both sides argued over whether the outlets violated journalistic standards and infringed on national security through their reporting. Kelly told attorneys he may issue a full ruling by Tuesday, when the current extension is set to expire.

Kelly appeared skeptical of the administration’s justification for the ban, at one point questioning if it went against journalistic standards to portray the Trump administration in a negative light.

The judge said different concepts had been “emitted into the air” to justify the government’s media ban as he continues to weigh whether to permanently reinstate the outlets.

Trump announced the ban in a Truth Social post last month.

“I am proud to announce that, effective immediately, I am banning Fake News CNN, MSNOW (who recently changed their name from MSNBC due to lack of viewership and credibility!), and Politico,” Trump wrote.

“Media Outlets shouldn’t be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they’re covering the President of the United States, the Trump Administration, or the United States of America. Other Fake News Media Outlets to follow.”

The outlets were then denied access to the White House grounds and had their hard passes revoked.

When asked about Trump’s timing on the ban following the announcement, he said it stemmed from “cumulative stories over the last few years” from reporters who “purposefully write negative news” about him and the administration.

He added: “I don’t want them in my office, I don’t want them here.”

In court, however, DOJ attorney Michael Velchik told the judge that Trump has concerns over journalistic standards, verifiable falsehoods and national security, as detailed in letters submitted to the court.

An attorney for the media outlets, Theodore Boutrous Jr., described the case as “textbook retaliation.”

The attorney then asked the judge to convert the temporary restraining order into a permanent injunction, restoring the credentials and hard passes of White House reporters.

Kelly issued the temporary order on Sept. 24 after the outlets sued the president and several White House officials, requesting their immediate reinstatement.

Kelly granted the order, writing the outlets would likely succeed in a lawsuit showing their hard passes were revoked without constitutionally adequate due process, the court filing states.

The White House argued the outlets endangered national security through their reporting, but Kelly did not find the circumstances “extraordinary.”

Additionally, he noted the government cannot revoke a reporter’s hard pass without explicitly stating the rules or standards governing reporter conduct that would lead to a revocation.

He also said the reporters would be entitled to “fair notice not only of the conduct that would subject him to punishment but also of the magnitude of the sanction that the White House might impose.”

Kelly remained “skeptical” as to whether the administration’s interest in safeguarding national security was the motivation behind the media ban, his initial ruling stated.

entries.title: Airbnb Disavows Anti-Trans Ad From Republican Super PAC It Supported
entries.summary: The company said it wasn’t aware of the signs — or the fact that the Airbnb logo would be displayed on them — before they were distributed.
entries.content:
Airbnb is denouncing a Republican super PAC’s anti-transgender campaign ad in Arizona, saying it wasn’t aware of the signs — or the fact that the Airbnb logo would be displayed on them — before they were distributed.

The controversial signs feature a girl on crutches with a bandaged leg along with the words: “Aaron Lieberman voted to put guys in girls' sports,” The Arizona Republic reported on Wednesday.

The placards were spotted in Arizona’s Legislative District 4, where Lieberman, a Democrat, is running against Republican incumbent state Sen. Carine Werner.

The Arizona Senate Victory Fund paid for the signs, according to the outlet.

Under Arizona law, PACs are required to disclose top donors on campaign signs. Airbnb donated $90,000 to the PAC between 2025 and 2026 — meaning the company’s logo had to be displayed at the bottom of the sign.

Still, Airbnb told the outlet it disagrees with the slogan.

“The message on this sign doesn't represent the views of Airbnb,” Lauren Bouton, a company spokesperson, told the newspaper. “We were not made aware of this campaign collateral in advance, nor do we have authority over ads produced by any third-party PAC that we contribute to in Arizona.”

The PAC, Airbnb and Lieberman did not immediately respond to a request for comment from The Washington Sun.

A website titled “The Truth About Lieberman” includes the same statement as the one on the sign, citing Arizona’s 2020 HB 2706, legislation that sought to restrict transgender students’ participation in sports teams that align with their gender identity. Lieberman, who previously served two terms in the Arizona Legislature, voted against the bill.

The legislation passed in the Arizona House of Representatives but did not become law.

An entrepreneur and business leader, Lieberman helped launch Jumpstart, a national early literacy nonprofit and co-founded Acelero Learning, which provides early education to prepare children for kindergarten, his campaign website states.

Werner describes herself as a “common-sense conservative.” She’s been in office since January 2025 and is running to “protect Arizona families, improve affordability, strengthen our schools, and ensure government works for the people it serves,” according to her campaign website.

entries.title: Susie Wiles and Her Daughter Met With Pro-Russia Balkan Officials, Photos Show
entries.summary: The photos resurfaced after Trump distanced himself from two advisers who traveled to the Republika Srpska region to advise its government ahead of the election.
entries.content:
White House chief of staff Susie Wiles and her daughter have separately met with senior figures from Bosnia’s pro-Russian Serb nationalist leadership in recent weeks, according to photos circulating online this week.

Photos documenting the Wiles’ meetings with members of the Republika Srpska, the autonomous entity that makes half of Bosnia and Herzegovina, surfaced after President Donald Trump distanced himself from two longtime political advisers over their travels to the region to advise its government on election-related issues.

Wiles met Željka Cvijanović, a close ally of longtime Bosnian Serb leader Milorad Dodik, at the White House on Sept. 21. Cvijanović posted a photo of the meeting on Instagram at the time, saying the two discussed “the situation in BiH and the region” and looked forward to continued cooperation.


HTML EmbedCvijanović won another term Sunday as the Serb member of Bosnia’s three-member presidency, and is a senior member of the SNSD, the Serb nationalist party that dominates Republika Srpska and maintains close ties with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Katie Wiles traveled to Republika Srpska in August and was photographed holding a rifle alongside the region’s interior minister, Željko Budimir, CBS News reported Thursday after verifying the image and its location.

Katie Wiles is a partner at Continental Strategy, a Washington lobbying firm that registered earlier this year to represent the Republika Srpska government. The firm told CBS that her two-day trip was for a separate U.S. client conducting a feasibility study and that she has not spoken with U.S. government officials about Republika Srpska.

A White House official sought to distance Susie Wiles from her daughter’s lobbying work, telling CBS News that “Susie does not discuss work matters with her daughters.”

The White House meeting between Susie Wiles and Cvijanović was arranged by Alex Garcia, another Continental Strategy partner who is registered to work for Republika Srpska.

Cvijanović said she and Wiles had agreed to continue talks within about a month to six weeks after their September meeting, and that she expected the discussions to lead to “concrete activities,” according to Republika Srpska’s government-linked news agency SRNA.

Trump distanced himself Wednesday from political advisers Chris LaCivita and James Blair and said he would “terminate them” if their outside work posed a conflict, after The New York Times reported that the two had traveled to Republika Srpska to advise its government on voting-related issues ahead of Oct. 4 election.

Republika Srpska has spent heavily on Washington lobbyists as its leaders have sought closer ties with the Trump administration. The administration last year lifted sanctions on Dodik and several of his allies that had been imposed over his efforts to undermine Bosnia’s U.S.-brokered postwar political order.

entries.title: Sen. John Fetterman Personally Invested in a Company Powering ‘Trump Accounts’
entries.summary: The Pennsylvania Democrat purchased up to $30,000 in Dell corporate bonds, according to a new congressional disclosure.
entries.content:
Sen. John Fetterman is personally investing in a company behind one of President Donald Trump’s signature priorities, according to a new congressional financial disclosure.

Fetterman (D-Pennsylvania) reported purchasing two corporate bonds in Dell, the computer company helping power Trump Accounts — the tax-advantaged financial accounts Trump’s administration is creating for every U.S. citizen child.

The corporate bonds, purchased three weeks ago, are each valued at between $1,001 and $15,000 and earmarked for at least one of his dependent children, the congressional disclosure indicates. (Lawmakers are only required to disclose the value of their transactions in broad ranges.)

Fetterman’s disclosure Wednesday coincided with an Oval Office event attended by Michael Dell, CEO of Dell Technologies, and his wife, Susan, celebrating children’s enrollment in the Trump Accounts program. Dell Technologies donated $6.25 billion to the project, which the Trump administration designed to give children “a big jump on life.”
Michael.Susan.Dell.Trump (8640x5760, AR: 1.50)The White House called the donation “one of the largest direct investments ever made in American families.” The Dell donation is expected to be invested across 25 million Trump Accounts accounts by Friday.

“Hopefully, we're not just giving them $250, we're giving them the beginning of an education and learning,” Dell told Yahoo! Finance.

The purchase follows criticism from Fetterman’s own party about his coziness with Republicans. Fetterman appeared by video to denounce socialism at Republicans’ midterm convention in September in Dallas.

After the cameo, Fetterman responded to speculation he’d switch parties by calling himself “a lifelong Democrat.” He told The Washington Sun: “Should the Senate flip in November, I will still be the 51st vote that I ran on.”

Fetterman’s Senate office didn’t respond to The Sun’s requests for comment on Thursday.

Earlier this year, Fetterman violated the Stop Trading on Congressional Knowledge Act when he was nearly a year late disclosing a financial trade made on one of his children’s behalf, The Sun reported. He told Senate officials the purchase was "inadvertently omitted” because of an "administrative error.”

Last week, Fetterman joined Senate Democrats in rejecting the proposed Stop Insider Trading Act, which would have prevented federal lawmakers from purchasing individual stocks.

Republicans had packaged the stock-purchase ban with an unrelated voter identification requirement, prompting Democrats to reject the bill during a procedural vote, even if many supported the stock ban in principle.

entries.title: Supreme Court Again Intervenes in Political Ad Rate Dispute
entries.summary: A lower court had given the FCC until Friday to resolve a dispute over the agency’s policy on television ad rates for parties coordinating with candidates.
entries.content:
The Supreme Court on Thursday once again quickly stepped into a legal clash regarding the rules governing the price of political television ads ahead of the midterms.

The Trump administration and Republican campaign committees asked the justices to halt a ruling from the 4th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, which gave the Federal Communications Commission until noon Friday to resolve a challenge from Democratic Senate nominees to the agency’s March guidance granting political party committees access to lower ad rates when coordinating with candidates.

Chief Justice John Roberts quickly did so — at least for now. He paused that 4th Circuit deadline while the Supreme Court considers the Trump request, and set a deadline of 5 p.m. Saturday for a response from the Democratic Senate nominees who brought the case, including Sen. Jon Ossoff of Georgia and former Sen. Sherrod Brown of Ohio.

The Trump administration, in an application to the court Thursday, called the initial 4th Circuit deadline a “flagrant abuse” of authority, pointing out that the Supreme Court last month stepped in to halt an earlier 4th Circuit ruling that paused the FCC guidance.

“In sum, just as the Fourth Circuit seriously erred when it first tried to leap-frog the Commission’s decision, it has now seriously erred in trying to short-circuit the Commission’s deliberations,” the Justice Department wrote.

In the lead-up to primary and general elections, candidates pay lower rates for television advertising than political parties — which can raise hundreds of thousands of dollars from a single donor — or outside groups such as super PACs, which can raise and spend unlimited amounts of money but cannot legally coordinate with candidates.

In June, the Supreme Court eliminated long-standing limits on coordinated spending between political parties and candidates, setting up the legal clash between the two political parties over whether they should be able to access the lower rate.

Last month, after the Supreme Court intervened to overturn the lower court’s pause, the FCC requested public comments on the Democratic nominees’ challenge on an expedited timeline, which closed Sept. 30. But because a broadcast association last month filed a separate challenge to the guidance with "overlapping issues," the FCCsaid it was consolidating the challenge and set another comment deadline of Oct. 19.

In the 2-1 decision on Wednesday, the 4th Circuit accused the FCC of “dragging its feet” and ordered the agency to resolve the dispute.

“We have heretofore accorded the FCC a substantial amount of grace, but its gamesmanship must end,” the judges wrote.

Republican party committees hold a significant cash advantage over their Democratic counterparts this election cycle, while Democratic candidates have outraised their Republican opponents in certain hotly contested races.

Political spending is picking up ahead of the Nov. 3 general election, and access to lower-cost television ad rates could help Republicans close the fundraising gap.

The National Republican Congressional Committee and the National Republican Senatorial Committee also asked the Supreme Court on Thursday to intervene before the deadline.

“If the case for a stay was strong the first time around, it’s open and shut now,” the party committees wrote in a separate emergency application.

entries.title: White House Floats Russ Vought’s Deputy to Lead Congress’ Watchdog Arm
entries.summary: OMB Deputy Director Eric Ueland has presided over massive shakeups to the federal workforce that the Government Accountability Office has deemed detrimental.
entries.content:
The White House has floated placing one of its top officials to serve as the head of the government’s most powerful watchdog, a move that could threaten the oversight of President Donald Trump’s overhaul of the executive branch.

Trump is considering nominating Office of Management and Budget Director Russ Vought’s deputy to serve as the nation’s comptroller general, the Government Accountability Office’s chief, for a 15-year term, according to four people familiar with the matter.

As OMB deputy director, Eric Ueland has presided over massive shakeups to the federal workforce and how agencies carry out their missions. Under Vought and Ueland, the administration has directed government spending and workforce changes that GAO has on several occasions deemed illegal and detrimental to the functioning of government.

If nominated and confirmed to lead the legislative branch’s watchdog agency, Ueland himself would get to decide whether to hold the administration accountable for work he previously was a part of.

The White House has raised the idea of nominating Ueland to Senate Republicans, who have an outsized role in the GAO leadership selection process. By statute, a bipartisan congressional commission must send at least three candidates to the president to consider for nomination. The top GAO job has sat vacant since Gene Dodaro’s term expired at the end of 2025.

In addition to his role at OMB, Ueland is serving as the acting director of the Office of Government Ethics and the largely defunct U.S. Agency for International Development. Ueland did not respond to requests for comment, and OMB declined to comment.

Trump’s push to install Ueland comes at a perilous time for GAO and its relationship with Congress. GAO is facing pressure from Capitol Hill to exercise its power to sue the Trump administration over what the watchdog itself has labeled illegal budgetary gimmicks, like impounding billions of dollars in congressionally approved funds over the last two years.

A post-Watergate law prohibits an administration from withholding congressionally appropriated funds for policy reasons. The law gave GAO the authority to sue an administration that improperly refuses to spend money, and recent court precedent has suggested only GAO has the authority to bring such a challenge.

The GAO has faced unusual resistance from federal agencies in seeking the documents and interviews necessary to conduct its audits and reviews. GAO typically launches investigations at the request of members of Congress, though the auditors have encountered increased resistance from requests originating from Democrats.

“Our agency access issues are worse than ever,” one GAO employee told The Washington Sun.

GAO, as recently as Tuesday, said the Trump administration has unlawfully refused to disburse funds that Congress previously appropriated. OMB has rejected GAO’s findings and said the watchdog has no authority over it anyway.

Last week, GAO found the Trump administration’s “pocket rescissions” of $800 million also amounted to a violation of spending law. The move allowed OMB to withhold funds until they expired at the end of the fiscal year.

Some lawmakers and their staff have raised concerns about GAO so far declining to bring any legal challenges to the Trump administration’s budgetary machinations to current leadership — who are serving in acting capacities — according to GAO and congressional staffers.
Susan Collins AP - 25198625293696 (4500x3000, AR: 1.50)They “have been vocally perturbed about the posture of our appropriations attorneys,” a GAO employee said, adding the feedback has come from both parties.

A Senate Republican aide confirmed there has been a push to get GAO to sue the administration, particularly after appropriators fended off an effort by the Trump administration to cut the watchdog agency’s budget in half.

"There’s been more and more interest in going about the legal route,” the Republican aide said. “Appropriators have protected GAO’s funding and are wondering why this isn’t happening.”

Placing a White House official into GAO leadership has the potential to end any threat of a lawsuit and to upend the watchdog agency altogether. Both the first and second Trump administrations have clashed with Congress’ watchdog, and Vought has suggested GAO should not exist. Vought issued guidance to agencies last year directing them to not be overly deferential to GAO.

The push to install an OMB appointee comes after a wide range of outside government groups, including the right-wing Americans for Prosperity and the libertarian R Street Institute, said Congress alone should have the authority to appoint a GAO chief and the president should have no role at all.

GAO has only sued over impoundments once — in 1975, one year after Congress passed the law deeming them illegal — but the matter was resolved before a judge could issue any ruling. Dave Walker, who led GAO from 1998 to 2008, sued the office of then-Vice President Dick Cheney over access to documents. A judge dismissed the case and Walker opted not to appeal, though he told The Washington Sun the George W. Bush administration worked well with his agency after that dustup.

Walker said he sought widespread buy-in before opting to launch his suit.

“I proactively reached out on both sides of the aisle and both ends of the Hill before I decided to sue and before I made my decision not to appeal,” Walker said.

Current GAO leadership — career staff serving in their roles temporarily — are unlikely to feel sufficiently empowered to sue the administration.

“When you’re acting, it’s not the same as being a confirmed comptroller general,” Walker said.

Frustration with GAO has also reached the ranks of its own workforce. Agency leadership demonstrated its cautious approach recently when it released new guidance to staff, reviewed by The Sun, on encountering agency resistance during investigations. The process involves setting an initial deadline, then a second if the first one is ignored and finally an internal elevation process if agencies continue to refuse to cooperate.

The watchdog’s counsel office will then strategize on a best path forward, though GAO supervisors are expected to engage further with agencies and, eventually, notify members of Congress who requested the report of the roadblocks. Top GAO leadership only gets involved 45 days after the second missed deadline, with guidance suggesting they will confer to figure out how to proceed.

Just getting to that point would take months, a GAO employee said, adding the analysts have little confidence in the agency’s lawyers.

“Without a smoking gun handed to them, they are relying on agencies to tattle on themselves,” the employee said. “Internally, we have effectively abandoned any hope of relying on them.”

The employee added that GAO leadership and its general counsel “are very wary about ever suing.”

“They don't want to lose and have GAO's authority diminished,” the employee said. “So instead, they just kinda don't flex our authority, which has the same effect.”

Publicly, Democratic lawmakers have said Republicans should work with them to pass legislative language that would prohibit pocket rescissions and impoundments.

“If Republicans are ready to grow a spine and help us rein in Trump on pocket rescissions — great, it’s way past time,” Sen. Patty Murray (D-Washington), the top Democrat on the Senate Appropriations Committee, said last week. “I am not holding my breath.”

The commission to select the next head of GAO has still not convened nine months after Dodaro’s departure, according to several sources familiar with the matter. Sen. Rand Paul (R-Kentucky), who in the current Senate makeup would serve as the de facto head of the commission under his role as chair of the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, did not respond to a request for comment but previously said he planned to take the process seriously.

The panel must suggest at least three candidates to lead GAO, and the president can subsequently request they come up with more names. The law does not explicitly require the president to choose from the commission’s list, though the White House has done so.

entries.title: Democratic Congressional Campaign Says DHS Claim It Hired a Criminal Is Bogus
entries.summary: The government cited a conservative media report alleging Janelle Stelson employed an illegal immigrant arrested for indecent exposure.
entries.content:
A Democratic congressional campaign in Pennsylvania says the Department of Homeland Security wrongly accused them of employing an undocumented immigrant who was arrested for indecent exposure and disorderly conduct.

DHS said in a news release on Wednesday that the suspect, Chimaobim Adedayo Igbojekwe, worked as a canvasser for Janelle Stelson, who is running against Republican Rep. Scott Perry in central Pennsylvania’s 10th Congressional District.

Stelson’s campaign adamantly denied Igbojekwe had any involvement in the campaign.

“This individual is not and has never been employed by the Janelle Stelson campaign,” Campaign Manager Alma Baker said in a statement Thursday. “If he is an illegal immigrant who committed a crime he should be deported. We never heard of him prior to the news of this arrest.”

DHS made the allegation in a press release that cited an article from the Shore News Network, a conservative outlet, in which Scott Presler, a conservative political activist, identified Igbojekwe as a canvasser for Stelson. Presler told the outlet that campaign flyers were found inside of Igbojekwe’s vehicle but did not immediately respond to a request for comment from The Washington Sun.

“It’s unbelievable that Janelle Stelson would employ an illegal alien to work on a Congressional campaign, let alone a pervert who exposed himself in public,”Charles Wall, deputy director for Immigration and Customs Enforcement, said in the news release.

DHS notes that Igbojekwe was granted deferred action by the Biden administration in 2021. The release does not offer any indication the federal government investigated Igbojekwe’s employment.

Federal campaigns are required to report the names of employees and their compensation. Igbojekwe does not appear in records of the Federal Election Commission.

The DHS office declined to answer further questions from The Sun about the allegation.

There have been cases where independent contractors have employed people who are not directly hired by campaigns. Still, asked if the Igbojekwe could have been hired by a contractor or might have worked as a volunteer, Baker said, “No. We never heard of him prior to the news of his arrest.”

The allegation surfaced as Stelson and Perry are locked in a race rated a “toss up.”

Stelson lost to Perry in 2024 by about 1 percentage point. The district is more competitive this year and Democrats think this year’s challenging political environment for the GOP could help them unseat the former Freedom Caucus chair.

entries.title: Trump Awards His Frenemy Elon Musk and Tech Allies With the National Medal of Science
entries.summary: The president called Musk an “industrial titan."
entries.content:
President Donald Trump continued to build on a cozy relationship with tech moguls on Thursday by awarding several of them the National Medal of Science — including his onetime critic Elon Musk.

Musk, the Tesla founder who formerly led DOGE under Trump, received the medal alongside Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, Google co-founder Sergey Brin and Advanced Micro Devices CEO Lisa Su. The National Medal of Technology and Innovation was awarded to Dell CEO Michael Dell and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella.

“Elon is our modern day Thomas Edison,” Trump said at the event, held at the U.S. Institute of Peace. “And I want to congratulate you. You are my friend and all that.”

Trump was presented with a National Medal of Science that had been awarded in the 1980s to his uncle John G. Trump for his work on high-voltage radiation methods.

The award is the highest recognition the president can present a scientist or engineer whose contributions have served the nation.

The technology industry — and AI specifically — has been central to Trump’s presidency. Musk donated $291 million to Republican candidates and PACs during the 2024 election cycle, according to OpenSecrets. Multiple tech CEOs attended Trump’s inauguration. Michael Dell and his wife, Susan Dell, pledged to donate $6.25 billion for the president’s “Trump Accounts” initiative.

Trump has been a major booster of data centers and what he calls “super intelligence,” dismissing warnings about the risks from AI leaders.

The president pushed to expand data center proposals and AI initiatives. Earlier this month, he launched a “super intelligence force” to lead the nation's AI advancement. Trump has allowed tech moguls to self-regulate their companies.

Meanwhile, Americans have opposed local data centers and shown a growing concern for AI advancement. According to Heatmap Pro, at least seven in 10 Americans said they would “oppose a data center being built near their home.” The Pew Research Center also found that 52% of Americans are concerned about the use of AI in daily life.

The presentation of the medal to Musk marks an improvement in his relationship with the president since their public fallout last year.

During Thursday’s event, Trump called Musk an “industrial titan” and highlighted his innovations at Tesla and SpaceX and the recent return of a SpaceX crew from the International Space Station.

“Quite honestly, there is no one like him,” Trump said about Musk.

entries.title: Senate Judiciary Democrats Demand Republicans Apologize for Jack Smith Hearing Debacle
entries.summary: The committee members accused their Republican colleagues of failing to provide materials connected to Sen. Eric Schmitt’s now-viral basketball team mix-up.
entries.content:
Senate Judiciary Democrats are demanding their Republican colleagues issue an apology to Jack Smith after a Missouri senator fumbled his questioning of the former Justice Department special counsel during a committee hearing last week.

Sen. Eric Schmitt (R-Missouri) tried to connect Smith — a former DOJ official best known for his 2022 prosecution of President Donald Trump — to a Georgia district attorney by blowing up photos of text messages that he thought placed Smith at a basketball game in Atlanta.

The 10 Democratic signatories said the committee’s Republican majority violated Senate rules by not sharing all records used to question Smith with the minority.

“We write to object to the Committee violating Senate rules by failing to provide committee records to the minority in advance of the hearing … As of the date of this letter, we still have not received these records,” the senators wrote in a letter addressed to committee chair Sen. Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa).

“We request that you immediately provide these and all other documents that you have withheld, commit to fully complying with Senate rules in the future, and apologize to Mr. Smith on behalf of the Committee for the unacceptable personal attacks and false accusations of perjury he faced during this hearing,” the letter said.

When The Washington Sun asked Grassley’s office if it plans to issue an apology to Smith, a spokesperson flagged a post on X in which the senator wrote that “Jack Smith should apologize for taking the bank records of 42 Iowans & 4,782 Americans.”

The Democratic signatories, led by ranking member Sen. Dick Durbin (D-Illinois), maintain that neither Schmitt nor Sen. Josh Hawley (R-Missouri) have produced documents related to their questioning of Smith — which they say constitutes a “particularly egregious breach” of Senate committee rules.

Schmitt tried to place Smith at an Atlanta Hawks game in February 2024 in an attempt to tie him to Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis, who launched an investigation into the president’s efforts to subvert the 2020 election results in Georgia.

The state court system disqualified Willis from the case after details emerged of her affair with Nathan Wade, the special prosecutor hired for the 2020 election interference case — a transgression Schmitt pointed out.

The Missouri Republican even had a large sign made showing text messages he thought placed Smith at the game next to large photos of Willis and Wade. Schmitt accused Smith of perjuring himself and said he would “go down as a total dirtbag.”

Smith appeared confused before Sen. Amy Klobuchar jumped in to assert that her Republican colleague had likely confused the Atlanta Hawks with the University of Iowa Hawkeyes. The clip of the incident circulated widely on the internet, with some senators appearing gobsmacked while watching the episode unfold.

“Jack Smith deserves an apology from my Republican colleagues who falsely accused him of perjury,” Durbin wrote Thursday on X. “This shameful episode was an embarrassment to the Committee that demands an explanation.”

Schimitt has attempted to downplay the viral gaffe.

“Who knew Jack Smith was a Caitlin Clark fan?” Schmitt told CNN. “We had information he was at a basketball game. There was only one NBA game that night which is why I asked him if he was in Atlanta.”

Smith has faced Trump’s fury for overseeing the investigations into the president’s retention of potentially classified materials, which led to a raid on his Mar-a-Lago estate in 2022. Smith also led the case against Trump for his efforts to overturn the 2020 election results and his part in the Jan. 6 attack on the U.S. Capitol.

entries.title: NFL to Supreme Court: States Should Regulate Prediction Markets
entries.summary: “This is about protecting game integrity and consumers,” an NFL spokesperson said.
entries.content:
The National Football League wants state regulators, not the federal government, to oversee and regulate prediction markets such as Kalshi, the league wrote in a Supreme Court filing Thursday.

The league, noting that “billions of dollars will be bet on NFL games through prediction markets each season,” asked the court to swiftly take up a federal case between Kalshi and New Jersey officials. Last month, New Jersey asked the same of the court.

The case could determine the fate of sports-related prediction markets, which have enjoyed what the NFL called a “laissez-faire approach” to safeguards and rules from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission in contrast to state gaming commissions’ often-rigid regulations.

The brief puts the NFL in opposition to the Trump administration, which this year has been suing states attempting to regulate prediction markets. The Trump family also has ties to Kalshi and its largest competitor, Polymarket, since Donald Trump Jr. is an adviser to both.

However, the NFL told The Washington Sun that it does not see the filing as an all-out attack on the burgeoning prediction market industry.

“This is not about the NFL opposing prediction markets,” NFL spokesperson Tim Schlittner said. “This is about protecting game integrity and consumers — just like legalized sports betting.”

Elisabeth Diana, chief of communications at Kalshi, told The Sun that the integrity of its markets is the company’s “top priority.” She said this is reflected in Kalshi’s partnerships with other sports behemoths, including Major League Baseball and the National Hockey League.
Kalshi (2733x3125, AR: 0.87)Diana did not respond when asked whether prediction markets could operate under the legal structure the NFL is pushing for.

In its Supreme Court brief, the NFL disagreed with an earlier decision from the 3rd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, where Kalshi successfully argued that the Commodity Futures Trading Commission was the “exclusive regulator” over financial contracts known as “swaps” — in this case, the event contracts traded between users.

The 6th and 9th circuit courts of appeal highlighted that the definition of “swap” has limits: specifically that it “must be inherently associated with a potential financial or economic consequence, not just that the event or contingency have some potential downstream financial consequence,” the brief states.

While Kalshi points to the Dodd-Frank Act giving the CFTC “exclusive jurisdiction” over swaps, the NFL wrote in the brief that it was "inconceivable" Congress’ response to the 2008 financial crisis enabled the “nationwide legalization of sports bets.”

“Any delay from the Court will result in increasing consumer harm and risk to game integrity,” the NFL wrote in the brief. The NFL made up half of prediction markets’ volume on the first Sunday of its season, the league wrote.

The NFL has repeatedly objected to certain sports-related contracts on prediction markets like Kalshi and Polymarket. In March, NFL chief compliance officer Sabrina Perel wrote a letter to prediction market operators asking that they scrap “objectionable bets,” CNBC reported.

Some were “inherently objectionable,” such as markets allowing contracts on whether an athlete would sustain an injury while others were too easy to manipulate, such as whether a football placekicker would miss a field goal, Perel wrote.

"It is deeply concerning that bets within the objectionable categories that we identified months ago have been and continue to be listed as contracts on exchanges,” Perel wrote in a follow-up last month.

Diana rebuffed the NFL’s framing, writing that the “CFTC is actively policing sports-related markets, which are now listed on every US commodities exchange.”

“The CFTC’s ongoing rulemaking addresses many of the NFL’s supposed concerns,” she wrote. “And those rules sit atop the same comprehensive system of federal enforcement that protects trillions of dollars of transactions in US markets.”

entries.title: Democrats Call for Kimberly Guilfoyle’s Removal After Bombshell Report
entries.summary: The U.S. ambassador to Greece sought $100,000 from a Trump donor while offering access to administration officials, according to a report published this week.
entries.content:
Democratic lawmakers are calling for Kimberly Guilfoyle, the U.S. ambassador to Greece, to be fired after a bombshell report that she sought $100,000 from a Trump donor while offering access to administration officials.

Rep. Gregory Meeks of New York, the top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, said that Guilfoyle should be removed if the allegations are true.

“Reports coming out regarding Amb. Guilfoyle’s conduct are deeply concerning and suggest potentially corrupt influences on U.S. foreign policy,” Meeks said in a statement to The Washington Sun.

“If these allegations are accurate, Amb. Guilfoyle is unfit to represent the United States abroad and should be removed from her position.”

A spokesperson for the Democratic staff of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee confirmed that they are requesting further information and continuing to investigate.

The Wall Street Journal⁠ reported Wednesday that Guilfoyle texted Trump donor Eric Deters, a former Kentucky congressional candidate, to ask if he would cover a $100,000 American Express bill before her Senate confirmation hearing in 2025.

The newspaper reported that Guilfoyle offered to help Deters with tax and legal matters by connecting him with Trump administration officials. She also suggested that the payment could be made without leaving a paper trail according to the WSJ. Deters did not ultimately make the payment and told the newspaper that Guilfoyle had been unable to make good on her promise of access to Trumpworld insiders.

Guilfoyle’s attorney, Jesse Binnall, disputed the authenticity of the messages but did not identify specific inaccuracies.

Guilfoyle, a former Fox News host and ex-fiancée of Donald Trump Jr., was confirmed as ambassador in September 2025.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio declined to address the allegations while leaving Greece on Thursday. He said he was aware of The Wall Street Journal's reporting but did not know whether the allegations were true. He declined to say whether the State Department would investigate.

Vice President JD Vance weighed in on the allegations Thursday, saying he opposed government officials selling access but he wanted to "get the full story before offering a real opinion."

"Of course I don't like anybody selling access to another government official, certainly a high-level government official," he added.

Rep. Don Beyer, a Virginia Democrat who previously served as a U.S. ambassador, said Guilfoyle should be removed and potentially face criminal charges.

“As you would expect, accepting large sums of cash in exchange for access or favors using her official position would obviously run afoul of these.” Beyer wrote on X.

“Ambassador Guilfoyle must be fired and if she broke the law, which seems highly likely, prosecuted.”

Other Democrats also condemned the alleged financial dealings.

Rep. James Walkinshaw, a Virginia Democrat, called for a Justice Department investigation.

“This should be investigated by the Department of Justice. If we had an independent Department of Justice, as we've had under Republican and Democratic administrations, this kind of thing would be investigated,” he said.

Reps. Dave Min of California and Raja Krishnamoorthi of Illinois, as well as Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland, also added their names to the list of lawmakers calling for a criminal investigation.

The new allegations follow earlier reports about Guilfoyle’s dealings with private businesses and foreign officials while serving as U.S. ambassador.

The Daily Mail reported Thursday that the State Department’s inspector general is investigating earlier allegations involving her treatment of embassy staff, use of private aircraft, acceptance of gifts and business relationships.

The Journal previously reported that Guilfoyle promoted the interests of a Greek energy and construction company, allowed its lobbyist to attend diplomatic meetings and suggested the U.S. could undermine Greece’s government.

Those reports had already prompted congressional scrutiny. In an Oct. 1 letter, Meeks demanded answers from Rubio about Guilfoyle’s conduct and any investigation, giving the department until Oct. 15 to respond.

Sen. Jeanne Shaheen of New Hampshire, the top Democrat on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, separately requested an immediate review.

Just hours before The Wall Street Journal story broke, Rubio defended Guilfoyle, telling reporters at a news conference in Athens, “Suffice it to say, our embassy here is doing a great job. Our ambassador has been a strong ambassador here.”

entries.title: SpaceX, Palantir, McDonald’s: Trump Made 517 Personal Financial Trades in August
entries.summary: Federal records detail the president’s latest stock and bond spree.
entries.content:
President Donald Trump made 517 personal trades of stocks, bonds or other financial funds in August, many disclosed past a federal deadline for publicly revealing them.

Trump disclosed a filing published Thursday by the independent Office of Government Ethics.

Trump made some multi-million-dollar adjustments to his portfolio in August, including purchases between $1 million and $5 million each in Microsoft, McDonald’s and Comcast stock.

Those trades are among the 125 that Trump reported late in violation of the Stop Trading on Congressional Knowledge Act, which he also violated last month when he separately disclosed 1,156 trades made in July.

Trump added heavily to his position in Meta Platforms; he bought between $5 million and $25 million on Aug. 21, his largest transaction in August. (Federal law only requires officeholders to disclose the value of each trade in broad ranges, not exact amounts.)

That same day, Trump ditched a slate of computer chip stocks — AMD, Nvidia, Broadcom and Microchip — and hardware and cybersecurity companies including Dell, CDW, Fortinet, Datadog, CrowdStrike, Vertiv and Ciena.

Those sales coincided with Trump’s purchases in the media, oil and telecommunications sectors, with buys in Chevron, ConocoPhillips, AT&T, Netflix, Disney and General Mills. The AT&T and Netflix purchases were each valued at between $1 million and $5 million.

A White House spokesperson previously told The Washington Sun that “President Trump’s stock and bond portfolio is independently managed by third-party financial institutions.”

Trump, however, personally signs off on his financial disclosures, indicating that he is personally aware of trades being made on his behalf and what stocks and bonds he owns.

The president has routinely bought and sold stocks of companies who do significant business with, or are heavily regulated by, the federal government. On Thursday, Trump accused Microsoft and Adobe — he owned stock in both companies, as of Aug. 31 — of fraud and barred them from receiving access to new green cards for foreign workers.

Trump’s Intel transaction, a sale valued at between $100,000 and $250,000, comes as the federal government has purchased a 10% stake in the company — an arrangement made by the Trump administration.

Trump bought between $1 million and $5 million in unsecured SpaceX corporate bonds. SpaceX has received billions of dollars in government contracts since Trump took office last year despite the president’s on-again, off-again relationship with its trillionaire owner, Elon Musk.

Trump is a big trader of health care stocks. In August, he bought shares in drug, vaccine and health device manufacturers — Pfizer, Moderna, Abbott, Medtronic, Stryker and Boston Scientific — while selling insurers such as UnitedHealth, Cigna and Alignment Healthcare.

The president also sold shares of Versant Media Group, the parent company of MS NOW, one of the networks Trump has tried to bar from the White House.
